questions.text: The time value of money concept states that:
options: Money has constant value over time
Money available today is worth more than the same amount in future
Future money is always more valuable than money today
Time has no impact on money value
questions.explanation: A rupee today can be invested to earn returns, making it more valuable than a rupee received later.

questions.text: Interval funds are:
options: Closed-end schemes that become open-ended during specified transaction periods
Schemes that can be bought only once a year
questions.explanation: Interval funds are a variant of closed-end funds that open for purchase and redemption at specified intervals for at least two days.

questions.text: Margin trading allows an investor to:
options: Borrow funds from broker to buy more securities than cash available, subject to regulations
questions.explanation: Margin trading is leveraged buying where part funding is provided by the broker within regulatory limits.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: Which of these steps helps avoid a debt trap?
options: Using credit cards for minimum payment only
questions.explanation: Emergency funds reduce reliance on borrowing during financial stress.

questions.text: Category I and II AIFs must be close-ended with minimum tenure of:
questions.explanation: Category I and II AIFs are close-ended schemes with a minimum tenure of three years.

questions.text: Savings ratio is defined as:
questions.explanation: It measures the proportion of income saved each year.

questions.text: An increasing net worth over successive years indicates:
options: Financial progress and accumulation of assets
questions.explanation: Growing net worth shows positive wealth creation.

questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about asset allocation is TRUE?
options: It has minimal impact on portfolio performance
It is the key determinant of long-term portfolio returns and risk
It focuses only on stock selection
It can be ignored once the portfolio is constructed
questions.explanation: Empirical studies show asset allocation is the major driver of a portfolio’s long-term risk and return.

questions.text: An intermediary found guilty of mis-selling or misconduct may face:
options: Suspension or cancellation of registration by SEBI
Tax penalty by Income Tax Department
questions.explanation: SEBI can suspend, cancel, or impose monetary penalties on intermediaries violating regulations.

questions.text: The most widely used risk-adjusted performance measure is:
questions.explanation: The Sharpe Ratio is the most popular risk-adjusted performance measure, assessing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: In terms of investor eligibility and minimum investment size, AIFs and PMS are generally:
options: Designed for retail investors with very small ticket sizes
Targeted at sophisticated or high-net-worth investors with higher minimum investment amounts
questions.explanation: Both AIFs and PMS typically require high minimum investments and are meant for sophisticated / HNI investors.

questions.text: A stock split means:
options: Company merges two shares into one
Company divides each share into smaller units to increase liquidity
Company issues new shares for cash
questions.explanation: A stock split divides shares into smaller units to make them more affordable and increase liquidity.

questions.text: Which of the following are the main segments of the Indian debt market?
options: Government securities, PSU and bank bonds, and corporate debt instruments
Only government securities and equity shares
Only treasury bills and commercial papers
Corporate equity, real estate and commodities
questions.explanation: The Indian debt market broadly comprises government securities (G-Secs and SDLs), PSU/bank bonds and private sector corporate debt instruments.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a fixed-income security?
options: An instrument providing variable cash flows without any legal obligation
An instrument that provides a pre-defined interest or coupon and principal repayment schedule
A pure ownership claim in a business
A contract whose value depends on an underlying asset but has no cash flows
questions.explanation: Fixed-income securities (like bonds) generally pay a stated coupon and repay principal at maturity, subject to default risk.

questions.text: Which of these best describes holistic financial planning?
options: Coordinating investments, insurance, tax, retirement and estate aspects around the client’s life goals
Keeping all money in a savings account
questions.explanation: Holistic planning considers all aspects of the client’s financial life and integrates them around their goals.

questions.text: Under a growth option in a mutual fund scheme:
options: Dividends are paid out regularly to the investor
Dividends, if declared, are reinvested as fresh units
Returns are retained in the scheme and reflected as higher NAV
The investor’s capital is returned each year
questions.explanation: In the growth option, income is retained in the scheme and leads to appreciation in NAV, which the investor realises on redemption.

questions.text: Depository Participants (DPs) function as:
options: Agents of depositories who open and maintain demat accounts for investors
questions.explanation: DPs act as agents of depositories for investors, opening demat accounts and facilitating securities transfers.

questions.text: Redemption proceeds can be credited to:
options: Any bank account of the investor’s relatives
Only the registered bank account linked to the folio
questions.explanation: Funds are credited only to the pre-registered bank account linked with the folio to prevent misuse.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding investor grievance handling?
options: Complaints can only be submitted physically
SCORES allows paperless digital complaint resolution
Investors must pay a fee to file on SCORES
questions.explanation: SCORES provides a free, paperless, and transparent process for investors to submit and monitor complaints online.

questions.text: If an investor is not satisfied with the intermediary’s response, they can approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can escalate unresolved complaints to SEBI via its online platform, SCORES.

questions.text: SEBI’s main functions are categorized under:
questions.explanation: SEBI performs regulatory, developmental, and protective roles to ensure transparent and efficient capital markets.

questions.text: Net Asset Value (NAV) per unit is calculated as:
options: Net assets divided by face value
Number of units divided by net assets
Net assets divided by number of outstanding units
Total investments divided by number of investors
questions.explanation: NAV per unit = Net assets / Number of outstanding units.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers can invest a maximum of ___% of a client’s portfolio in their own associate or related companies.
questions.explanation: As per SEBI, the cap is 30% with prior written consent from the client.

questions.text: If monthly expenses are ₹60,000 and liquid assets ₹2,40,000, the liquidity ratio equals:
For mutual fund investors, the first point of contact for grievances is:
options: The concerned AMC or its Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)
questions.explanation: Investors should first approach the AMC or its RTA; unresolved issues can then be escalated to SEBI through SCORES.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about futures and options is TRUE?
options: Both require mandatory delivery of underlying asset
Futures carry symmetrical risk, options provide asymmetric payoffs
Futures are cheaper than options in all cases
questions.explanation: Futures expose both parties to symmetric risk and reward, while option buyers have limited downside and unlimited upside.

questions.text: In the investor life cycle, the 'accumulation phase' is characterized by:
options: High net worth and focus on capital preservation
Building assets with higher risk tolerance and long horizon
questions.explanation: In the accumulation phase, investors are early in their careers, taking higher risk to build wealth over a long horizon.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must not accept funds or securities worth less than:
questions.explanation: The minimum threshold of ₹50 lakh applies to each client’s investment under PMS.

questions.text: Why is documentation of the financial plan important?
options: To avoid any future changes to the plan
To create a clear record of recommendations, assumptions and responsibilities
questions.explanation: Writing the plan ensures clarity, accountability and provides a reference for future review.

questions.text: Which entity manages the portfolio and day-to-day operations of a mutual fund scheme?
questions.explanation: The Asset Management Company (AMC) manages the scheme, including investments, marketing and investor servicing.

questions.text: A client wanting to retire early at age 50 instead of 60 will generally need to:
options: Save more and invest more aggressively in earlier years
questions.explanation: Early retirement means fewer earning years and more retired years, requiring higher saving and often more growth-oriented investments.

questions.text: Spread risk in credit markets is the risk that:
options: The yield difference between a corporate bond and a government bond of similar maturity widens
The difference between coupon and face value increases
The bid-ask spread in equity markets narrows
questions.explanation: Spread risk is the risk that the credit spread over government securities widens due to perceived higher risk, lowering bond prices.

questions.text: An open-ended mutual fund scheme:
options: Allows purchase only during the NFO period
Is for a fixed term and then compulsorily redeemed
Allows continuous purchase and redemption at prevailing NAV
Cannot be bought by retail investors
questions.explanation: Open-ended schemes issue and redeem units on a continuous basis at the applicable NAV and normally operate in perpetuity.

questions.text: The Indian banking system is regulated by:
questions.explanation: RBI is the regulator and supervisor of the banking system and monetary authority.

questions.text: Net assets of a mutual fund scheme are defined as:
options: Face value of units multiplied by number of units
Total assets minus total liabilities and expenses of the scheme
Total market value of securities only
Total cash balance in bank accounts
questions.explanation: Net assets are arrived at by taking the current value of the portfolio plus current assets and subtracting expenses and liabilities of the scheme.

questions.text: Which of the following is an ethical way to communicate expected returns?
options: Guaranteeing a fixed return above FD rates
Showing past performance with clear disclaimers that returns are not guaranteed
Promising that losses will never occur
questions.explanation: Ethical communication must be balanced, factual, and include disclaimers that past performance does not guarantee future returns.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines present value?
options: Current equivalent of a future amount discounted at an appropriate rate
Sum of principal and interest earned
questions.explanation: Present value is the amount that needs to be invested today to reach a desired future value, given a rate and time.

questions.text: Which of the following is the LEAST liquid asset in general?
questions.explanation: Direct real estate is typically illiquid; sale can take time and involve high transaction costs.

questions.text: Which statement about NBFCs is TRUE?
options: They can issue cheques like banks
They are allowed to accept demand deposits
They engage in lending and financial services but cannot accept demand deposits or issue cheques
They are regulated by SEBI only
questions.explanation: NBFCs undertake lending and other financial services but cannot accept demand deposits or issue cheques.

questions.text: The 50-30-20 rule for budgeting suggests allocating:
questions.explanation: A common thumb-rule: 50 % essentials, 30 % discretionary, 20 % savings.

questions.text: Depositories in India:
options: Hold securities in electronic form and update investor holdings
Act as brokers and execute trades
questions.explanation: NSDL and CDSL hold demat securities and record ownership electronically.

questions.text: Which is an example of good debt?
options: Loan to buy depreciating asset on EMI
questions.explanation: Borrowing for education or business that enhances earning potential is considered good debt.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key feature of Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)?
options: Units can be purchased only from the AMC at NAV end-of-day
They are listed and traded on stock exchanges like shares
They do not track any index or asset
questions.explanation: ETFs are mutual funds whose units are listed and traded on stock exchanges and typically track an index or asset.

questions.text: ‘Fiduciary duty’ implies that an adviser must:
options: Place client interest above their own and avoid conflicts
questions.explanation: A fiduciary must act with utmost good faith, prioritizing client interest above personal or organizational gain.

questions.text: Minimum net worth required for registration of a Portfolio Manager under SEBI (2020) Regulations is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: Liquidity risk for a bond investor is the risk that:
options: Coupons will be reinvested at higher rates
The bond cannot be sold quickly at a fair price due to thin trading
questions.explanation: Liquidity risk is the difficulty of finding ready buyers or sellers without significantly impacting the bond’s price.

questions.text: Which regulator handles insurance-related investor complaints?
questions.explanation: IRDAI regulates insurance entities and handles insurance-related grievances.

questions.text: Budget variance occurs when:
options: Actual figures differ from budgeted figures
All bills are paid on time
questions.explanation: Variance = Actual − Budgeted; it helps monitor deviations.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a category of AIF under SEBI regulations?
questions.explanation: There are only three categories of AIF — Category I, II and III.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common equity derivative traded on Indian exchanges?
options: Index futures and options on Nifty 50 and Sensex
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives such as Nifty 50 and Sensex futures/options are widely traded on NSE and BSE.

questions.text: A person’s monthly income = ₹80,000, fixed expenses = ₹30,000, variable = ₹40,000. What’s monthly surplus?
Which of the following complaints is typically NOT handled through SCORES?
questions.explanation: SCORES addresses regulatory or procedural violations; mere dissatisfaction with performance does not qualify.

questions.text: Estimation risk refers to:
options: The possibility that investors misestimate expected returns, risks, or correlations
questions.explanation: Estimation risk arises when input estimates (returns, risks, correlations) used in portfolio construction are inaccurate.

questions.text: Regulatory constraints are most likely to apply when:
options: The investor wants to invest abroad under LRS limits
The investor invests only in mutual funds
questions.explanation: Under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 overseas annually—this acts as a regulatory constraint.

questions.text: The main cost associated with frequent rebalancing is:
questions.explanation: Rebalancing involves brokerage and tax implications from buying and selling securities.

questions.text: The interest rate that includes all fees and charges to show total borrowing cost is called:
questions.explanation: APR reflects the true cost of borrowing including processing fees.

questions.text: The SCORES platform was launched by SEBI in:
questions.explanation: SEBI launched the SCORES (SEBI Complaints Redress System) in 2011 to digitize grievance handling.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly lists equity shareholder rights?
options: Voting rights, dividend entitlement, right to information
Only right to capital repayment before others
questions.explanation: Shareholders enjoy voting rights, dividends (if declared), and rights to company information.

questions.text: Which of the following events is LEAST likely to trigger a review of a financial plan?
options: Minor fluctuation in one month’s expenses
questions.explanation: Small short-term expense fluctuations are normal; major life or financial changes warrant a plan review.

questions.text: A callable bond is one where:
options: The investor can redeem early at a predetermined price
The issuer has the right to redeem the bond before maturity
The coupon rate changes automatically with inflation
The bond has no maturity date
questions.explanation: Callable bonds give the issuer the right to redeem the bond prematurely, usually when interest rates fall, increasing reinvestment risk for investors.

questions.text: Which channel most directly involves the Registered Investment Adviser (RIA) in the investment decision?
options: Client buying direct equity on their own without advice
Client investing in a mutual fund through a distributor only
Client taking model portfolio advice from an RIA and investing accordingly
Client keeping all money in a savings bank account
questions.explanation: Here, the RIA provides customised advice or model portfolios that the client implements, reflecting the advisory role specified by SEBI’s IA regulations.

questions.text: The 'consolidation phase' in the investor life cycle is typically when:
options: Income exceeds expenses and focus shifts to capital preservation
The investor depends entirely on investment income
The investor is gifting wealth to heirs
questions.explanation: In the consolidation phase, income exceeds expenses, and investors begin emphasizing capital preservation.

questions.text: From an advisory perspective, why is understanding different asset classes important?
options: To match assets with client’s goals, risk profile and time horizon
To help the client avoid diversification
To recommend only one product to all clients
questions.explanation: Advisers must understand asset characteristics to recommend suitable portfolios aligned to each client’s goals and risk tolerance.

questions.text: A 'risk-averse' investor will:
options: Always choose the highest return regardless of risk
Prefer investments with lower risk for a given return
Ignore the level of risk while investing
questions.explanation: Risk-averse investors prefer lower risk for a given return and demand a risk premium for taking additional risk.

questions.text: Redemption proceeds of NRI investments made on a non-repatriable basis are credited to:
questions.explanation: Non-repatriable proceeds are credited to the NRO account of the NRI investor.

questions.text: Credit counselling agencies help borrowers by:
options: Advising on debt management and repayment plans
questions.explanation: They guide borrowers on budgeting, negotiations and repayment discipline.

questions.text: Gift or inducement from product manufacturers to advisors can be unethical when:
options: It does not influence advice in any way
It causes bias in advice or is not disclosed where required
It is given at industry events
questions.explanation: Undisclosed gifts or inducements that bias advice create clear conflicts of interest and are unethical.

questions.text: A Follow-on Public Offer (FPO) refers to:
options: First issue of shares by a new company
Subsequent issue of shares by a listed company to the public
Private sale of shares between promoters
questions.explanation: FPO is a public issue by a company that is already listed on a stock exchange.

questions.text: Discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Execute client trades only after client approval
Have full discretion to manage funds as per the agreed mandate
Can act as mutual fund distributors
questions.explanation: Discretionary Portfolio Managers manage and invest client funds independently as per the client’s mandate.

questions.text: In India, derivatives trading is regulated by:
options: SEBI under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act
questions.explanation: Derivatives trading on exchanges is governed by SEBI under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.

questions.text: Which statement about emergency funds is MOST appropriate in the context of financial planning?
options: They are optional for salaried individuals
They should ideally cover 3 to 6 months of essential expenses
They should always be invested in equity funds
They are required only close to retirement
questions.explanation: A commonly used rule of thumb is to maintain 3–6 months of essential expenses in liquid form as an emergency fund.

questions.text: The primary role of a SEBI-registered Investment Adviser (RIA) is to:
options: Provide objective, fee-based investment advice suited to the client’s profile
Act as issuer of equity shares
Ensure all primary market issues are fully subscribed
questions.explanation: RIAs provide regulated, objective investment advice, considering the client’s risk profile and goals; they do not guarantee returns.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about standard deviation in portfolio theory?
options: It measures the average return of a portfolio
It measures dispersion of returns around the mean
It is always equal to variance
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance and measures the dispersion of returns around the mean.

questions.text: Debt restructuring refers to:
options: Revising loan terms to make repayment easier
questions.explanation: It may involve extending tenure, reducing rate, or partial waiver to restore repayment ability.

questions.text: Creating a household budget helps primarily to:
options: Identify surplus or deficit and control spending
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps monitor expenses and ensures planned savings.

questions.text: Which of the following asset classes generally has the highest short-term price volatility?
questions.explanation: Equities are typically the most volatile in the short term compared to the other options listed.

questions.text: Investment, in the context of personal finance, primarily refers to:
options: Holding cash in a locker for emergencies
Committing money to assets expected to generate income or capital growth
Spending on lifestyle items such as vacations and gadgets
Payment of income tax to the government
questions.explanation: Investment involves deploying money into assets with an expectation of future income and/or capital appreciation, not mere spending or idle cash.

questions.text: Correlation coefficient ranges between:
questions.explanation: Correlation values range between -1 and +1, where -1 indicates perfect negative and +1 perfect positive correlation.

questions.text: Market risk in the context of bonds primarily refers to:
options: Risk of default on coupon payment
Risk of change in bond prices due to changes in interest rates
Risk of not finding a buyer for the bond
questions.explanation: Market risk for bonds mainly arises from interest rate movements, which cause inverse changes in bond prices.

questions.text: A 25-year-old with no dependants and stable income is generally more suitable for which allocation?
options: Very high proportion of assets in cash only
Higher allocation to growth assets such as equity
questions.explanation: With long time horizon and low dependants, growth assets like equity can form a higher proportion of the portfolio.

questions.text: Which budgeting method allocates funds first to essential expenses and savings before discretionary spending?
questions.explanation: Pay-yourself-first ensures savings are prioritised before optional spending.

questions.text: Investors must update change in address or bank details:
questions.explanation: KYC-linked changes such as address and bank details must be updated with the KRA, which auto-updates all linked AMCs.

questions.text: The Principal Officer of a Portfolio Manager must have:
options: Minimum 5 years relevant experience and valid NISM certification
At least 10 years of audit experience
A postgraduate degree in economics only
questions.explanation: The Principal Officer must have at least 5 years’ experience in portfolio management, advisory, or related activities and hold NISM certification.

questions.text: Churning of client portfolios refers to:
options: Rebalancing as per agreed asset allocation
Excessive buying and selling primarily to earn higher fees or commissions
Investing in multiple funds for diversification
Switching from regular to direct plans
questions.explanation: Churning is unethical when trades are executed unnecessarily to generate more brokerage or fees, not to benefit clients.

questions.text: A top-up loan refers to:
options: Loan taken in addition to existing loan on same collateral
questions.explanation: Top-up allows borrower to access additional funds against same property.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a conflict of interest?
options: Advisor’s personal or financial interest clashing with duty to client
questions.explanation: A conflict of interest arises when the advisor’s personal or financial interests may compromise objective advice to the client.

questions.text: Which of the following helps investors verify whether their intermediary is SEBI-registered?
options: SEBI’s online intermediary database on its website
questions.explanation: Investors can verify intermediary registration on SEBI’s official website under the ‘Intermediaries / Market Infrastructure Institutions’ section.

questions.text: If the Sharpe Ratio of a portfolio is less than that of the market, it indicates:
options: Portfolio underperforms on a risk-adjusted basis
questions.explanation: A lower Sharpe Ratio than the market indicates inferior risk-adjusted performance.

questions.case_text: Amit and Neha, both aged 30, earn ₹1,00,000 per month jointly. They wish to buy a house worth ₹60 lakh in 5 years and also start saving for retirement at 60. Their current savings are ₹5 lakh invested in bank FDs. They can save ₹25,000 per month. Inflation is 6% p.a.

questions.text: Which of the following is Amit and Neha’s short-term goal?
questions.explanation: Emergency fund (3–6 months expenses) is short-term.

questions.text: Buying the house in 5 years is best categorised as a:
questions.explanation: Goals 3–7 years away are medium-term.

questions.text: Retirement planning is a ______ goal.
questions.explanation: Retirement lies 30 years ahead — a long-term goal.

questions.text: Their total monthly saving rate is:
To beat inflation over long term, they should allocate more to:
questions.explanation: Equities have potential to outperform inflation over long horizons.
